title: Canada Fast-Tracks Citizenship for Students as Processing Times Hit 25 Months
excerpt: An urgent processing route lets eligible applicants receive their citizenship certificate in time for the school semester, even as a post-Bill C-3 surge has overwhelmed standard timelines.
body:
• Canada is expediting proof of citizenship applications for people planning to study in the country, even as standard processing times have climbed to 25 months
  • The surge in applications follows Bill C-3, which removed the first-generation limit on citizenship by descent in December 2025, opening the door for millions abroad
  • Applicants must submit a cover letter requesting urgency and proof of enrollment at a Canadian institution alongside their full application
  • Canadian citizens pay domestic tuition rates, which can save thousands of dollars annually compared to international student fees

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada is fast-tracking proof of citizenship applications for people who need their certificates to study in the country, offering a rare shortcut as standard processing times stretch to 25 months, according to CIC News.

The expedited route is one of several "urgent processing" categories IRCC maintains for applicants facing time-sensitive situations. For students, the fast track can mean receiving a citizenship certificate in time for their starting semester — a timeline that would be impossible under regular processing.

Why Applications Have Piled Up

The backlog traces directly to Bill C-3, which removed the first-generation limit on Canadian citizenship by descent when it took effect on December 15, 2025. The change opened the door for millions of people abroad — many of them in the United States — to claim Canadian citizenship through a Canadian parent or grandparent.

"The expedited route is one of several "urgent processing" categories IRCC maintains for applicants facing time-sensitive situations."

Processing times have risen steadily throughout the past year and now sit at 25 months as of August, according to IRCC data. Some applicants who requested urgent processing on other grounds, including LGBTQ Americans citing safety concerns, have reported receiving their certificates in as little as two weeks.

How to Request Expedited Processing

To qualify on education grounds, applicants must submit three pieces of documentation alongside their complete proof of citizenship application: a cover letter requesting urgent processing and citing the relevant category, a letter explaining why expedited processing is needed and how it connects to their education, and proof of enrollment in a Canadian institution such as a letter of acceptance and a tuition summary.

An IRCC officer then decides whether the request qualifies. The department cautions on its website that it cannot guarantee the certificate will arrive in time, and incomplete applications will not be processed regardless of urgency.

Tuition Savings — and Catches

The financial incentive is significant. Canadian citizens generally pay domestic tuition, which can save thousands of dollars per year compared to international student rates. But there are complications. Some provinces, including Quebec, charge non-residents a higher tuition rate even when they hold Canadian citizenship — lower than international fees but above what in-province residents pay.

There is also a timing issue. Schools require a citizenship certificate on file before applying the domestic rate. Students whose applications are still processing may need to pay international tuition initially and seek adjustments once their certificate arrives.

Beyond Tuition

Education is one of several grounds IRCC considers for urgent processing. Others include avoiding harm linked to race, religion, nationality, or sexual orientation; bringing a minor child to Canada; resolving statelessness; family medical emergencies; meeting a foreign citizenship renunciation deadline; and employment needs.

Canadian citizenship also carries broader benefits. Citizens can work unlimited hours while studying, compared to the 24-hour weekly cap for international students on study permits. Those under 30 or 35 can access over 35 countries through International Experience Canada. And since both Canada and the United States allow dual citizenship, claiming Canadian nationality does not require giving up American citizenship.

What's Next

With processing times unlikely to shrink soon given the ongoing post-Bill C-3 surge, the urgent processing route may be the most practical path for anyone with Canadian ancestry who is planning to study in the country. IRCC reviews each request on its own merit, so applicants should ensure their documentation clearly establishes the education-related need.
nri_angle: Indian Americans with Canadian ancestry can use the fast-track route to claim Canadian citizenship for education, benefiting from domestic tuition rates and dual citizenship with both countries.
